Fact: The paper that started the current wave of AI is called Attention Is All You Need, published in 2017 by 8 researchers at Google.
Backbone: The thing running your feed, your inbox and half your tools traces to 1 paper younger than most people's cars. You are not late to this.

Fact: The word robot was invented for a stage play. Karel Capek used it in R.U.R. in 1920, from the Czech robota, meaning forced labour.
Backbone: We named the machines after the work nobody wanted to do, a century before we had any. The naming came first, the same way it does now.

Fact: ELIZA, one of the first chatbots, ran at MIT in 1966 and did little more than turn your own words back at you. Its author wrote that some people were very hard to convince it was not human.
Backbone: The problem was never that it understood. It was that being asked anything at all was rare enough to feel like being heard.
Source: Joseph Weizenbaum, Communications of the ACM, January 1966
